summary: The client WorldSync synchronization component.

evidence.text: WorldSync uses deterministic per-remote-player shader hue values, rather than modulation colors, as canonical identity values.

WorldSync intentionally keeps the local visual position unwrapped by accumulating shortest wrapped deltas. It moves the local Player node toward that position, and the camera follows the node. Backgrounds are not rebased; they use the player’s global position as shader scroll offset, which appears intended to support unwrapped coordinates. Remote-player and bullet targets are local-relative; asteroids maintain independent visual continuity after first sighting; indicators use rendered remote-player positions. The most likely cause of remote flashing was stale rendered state remaining in an old visual-copy family while a new local-relative target moved to another, causing interpolation across thousands of pixels.

WorldSync currently reads server player positions into target_player_positions, applies or interpolates them onto player nodes, and directly assigns server positions on initial spawn. _apply_players() processes local and remote players, including self_id, in the same loop. The gameplay camera is at Player/Camera2D inside the local player scene, while gameplay UI is at GameLoop/CanvasLayer/HUD. osindicator.tscn has a Control root and TextureRect child, percentage anchors, and a 128×128 child minimum size; it lacks an attached script and explicit visibility, mouse-filter, and pivot setup.
